newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian car market sees worst Sept in 12 years.
newsitem.headline: Italian car market sees worst Sept in 12 years.

text.p: The Italian car market reported its worst September for 12 years on Thursday amid growing gloom for the outlook on new car sales for the whole of 1996, while sales in most other European sales continued to grow.

Italian new registrations fell 8.5 percent last month to 116,000 from year ago levels after a 7.5 percent August fall, with car forecasting body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) saying it was now looking for a four percent fall in 1996 car sales from a previous flat estimate.

The poor state of the Italian car market was in sharp contrast to the whole European car market in September which grew 12.3 percent with 964,200 registrations, and by 16 percent when stripping out the poorly-performing Italian market.
CSP director Gian Primo Quagliano said he had revised down his forecast made at the start of the year for a 1996 total of 1.73 million new car registrations, unchanged from 1995 levels.

"Now we are expecting a four percent fall to 1.67 million vehicles," he told Reuters. "The market was in a phase of stagnation until July and showed a clear downward trend in August and September," he added.

CSP's latest monthly report showed that 49 percent of Italian car dealers expect sales to fall in the next three to four months, while 42 percent of those polled expected no change. Only nine percent saw sales increasing.

Italian car importers' association Unrae said the sharp fall in September confirmed a worrying drop in orders and pointed to a further slide in the last quarter of this year and forecast total 1996 sales well below last year's 1.7 million vehicles.

Bob Barber, car industry analyst at HSBC James Capel, was not as pessimistic as some Italian forecasters pointing out that August and September 1995 were strong months, and he saw the overall Italian market down only 1.5-2.0 percent in 1996.
"The real test will come in October when the corresponding month last year was weak. So we are fairly confident October sales will be up," he added.
The whole European car market hit the floor in 1993, but while other markets recovered, Italy has continued depressed weakening by a lack of consumer confidence.

In marked contast, other European car markets faired better. Provisional data showed booming sales in France where they were up 86 percent to over 216,000 cars in September, the last month valid for car-scrapping incentives.
In Spain, where the government has reduced car registration taxes, sales rose 18.6 percent, while in Germany sales rose just 1.0 percent, but in Britain they fell 2.0 percent.

Fiat's September Italian sales were affected by the poor state of the market and the launch of its new medium-large Marea car range in mid-month which limited new registrations. Fiat's Italian market share fell to 41.16 percent from 46.72 percent.
But orders from Italian dealers totalled 16,000 and would significantly influence data from October onwards, Fiat said.

Meanwhile, Fiat car sales were showing a marked improvement in Europe despite problems on the Italian market where group sales fell 17.5 percent year-on-year in September. Fiat group marques saw sales in Europe up 41.47 percent in September.
The positive trend in Europe was confirmed by figures for the January-September period with Fiat car sales up 23.7 percent in a European market which grew 8.0 percent, excluding Italy.
